title: Documenting and automating the repetitive parts of your business
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: List the systems your business needs, from enquiry to payment
Prioritise the automation with the most time saved
Test each automated process before relying on it

instruction.heading: Document everything you repeat
instruction.body: Each time you do a task more than twice, write it down. A one-page document and a short recorded walk-through are often enough. The aim is that someone else could pick the process up.

instruction.heading: Master systems list
instruction.body: List every process: enquiry, quote, booking, reminders, job checklist, invoicing, payment and review requests. Visibility comes first.

instruction.heading: Prioritise
instruction.body: Automate the processes that save the most time or prevent the most errors. Leave rare or complex processes until later.

instruction.heading: Build simply
instruction.body: Use the tools you already have, such as a calendar, a booking form, invoicing software and a shared document. A virtual assistant can run parts of the process. Keep the system simple enough to explain in a few minutes.

instruction.heading: Test before you rely on it
instruction.body: Run a test booking or test invoice through the whole process. Check the reminders, the payment and the record. Keep manual checks until the automation has worked several times.

procedure: Write every repeated task on one list.
Score each task for time saved and error risk.
Document the top three tasks as one-page procedures.
Automate one task at a time, starting with the highest score.
Test the process with a test booking and record the result.

workedExamples.situation: A handyman spends an hour a week sending reminders and chasing invoices by hand.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which process should be automated first?
workedExamples.reasoning: Invoice and reminder follow-up saves time and prevents late payment, so automate it first, then test it with a test invoice.

commonErrors.error: Automating before the process is clear
commonErrors.prevention: Document and check the manual process first.
Keep a periodic manual check of the records.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Document, prioritise, build simply, then test.
Automation should save time without hiding errors.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do before automating a process?
options: Buy the software with the most features, before any review
Remove all manual checks before the software is tested
Document it and check that the manual process works
Hire a new employee for the process before any review

knowledgeChecks.question: Which process should be automated first?
options: The rarest process, which happens only at year end
The most complex process in the whole business today
The process you enjoy most at the start of the day
One that saves the most time or prevents the most errors

knowledgeChecks.question: How should an automated process be tested?
options: With a test booking or test invoice through the whole process
By trusting the vendor and the vendor's promises in the brochure
By turning off the records and running it on old data
By asking a customer to test it on a busy Monday morning

knowledgeChecks.question: Which processes does the lesson list to be included in the systems list?
options: Enquiry, quote, booking, reminders, job checklist, invoicing, payment and review requests
